prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: There is a barrier among the egghead and (1)/ the hoipolloi and it would be lazy (2)/ idealism to ignore it. (3)/ No error (4)
options: There is a barrier among the egghead and
the hoipolloi and it would be lazy
explanation: 'Between' is used with two distinct parties, so it should be 'a barrier between the egghead and the hoipolloi.'

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The main purpose of the visit (a)/ is to develop a close relationship (b)/ among the two countries, (c)/ no error (d)
options: The main purpose of the visit
is to develop a close relationship
explanation: With exactly two items 'between' is required: 'between the two countries,' not 'among.'

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: These customs are (a)/ prevalent between the inhabitants of (b)/ the lower regions, (c)/ no error (d)
explanation: For more than two (a group of inhabitants) use 'among': 'prevalent among the inhabitants.'

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: He was the fastest between all the contestants.
explanation: 'All the contestants' is more than two, so 'between' must be replaced by 'amongst' (among).

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: There is an old rivalry between the three families for ages.
explanation: Three families is more than two, so 'among the three families' is required instead of 'between.'

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Among you and me / she is quite rude / to the boy.
explanation: Two persons ('you and me') require 'between', and the pronoun stays objective: 'Between you and me.'

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Ria's mother equally divided the chocolates among both her daughters.
explanation: 'Both her daughters' means two people, so 'among' must be replaced by 'between.'

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Their father has left (a)/ behind a huge sum to be (b)/ distributed among the two brothers, (c)/ No error (d)
options: behind a huge sum to be
explanation: 'Among' is used for more than two; with only two brothers the correct preposition is 'between'. Read 'distributed between the two brothers'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: If all of you quarrel (a)/ among yourself we shall not (b)/ be able to solve your problems, (c)/ No error (d)
options: be able to solve your problems,
explanation: A reciprocal action by several people needs the plural reflexive, so 'among yourself' must become 'among yourselves'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The principal distribution of tasks (A) / was carried out between (B) / all the members of the administrative cell. (C) / No Error (D)
options: all the members of the administrative cell.
explanation: 'Between' is used for two persons or things; for more than two, 'among' is required: 'was carried out among all the members'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: In geography class, / the teacher told the students, / "Switzerland lies / inside Germany, France, Austria, and Italy."
options: inside Germany, France, Austria, and Italy.
explanation: Switzerland lies 'between' (not 'inside') the four named countries, as clearly separate places are being referred to.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. They had two bedrooms among them, one for the girls and one for the boys.
explanation: 'Among' is used for more than two; for the two people implied here 'between them' is correct.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: If no substitution is required, select No improvement. An old misunderstanding exists among the two families , so they are not friendly any more.
options: has exist within the two families
will exist among the two families
explanation: 'Between' is used for two entities, so 'between the two families' is correct, and the singular subject 'misunderstanding' needs 'exists'.

prompt: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case
sentence: no improvement is needed select ‘No improvement required’. Fierce competition against restaurants has driven up the prices.
explanation: Competition involving more than two restaurants requires 'among', not 'against'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
sentence: She walked among me without greeting me.
explanation: 'Walked past me' expresses passing by; 'among' is used with three or more things and makes no sense here.

prompt: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case
sentence: no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Jack being the wiser and bolder among the two of us, took the lead, carrying the axe on his shoulder.
explanation: 'Between' is used for two persons/things ('the two of us'), and the comparative degree 'bolder' is correct for two.
